To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maternal diet enriched with n-3 PUFAs affects the fatty-acids composition of female piglet via the activation of lipogenic enzymes Δ6-desaturases (Δ6d) and Δ5-desaturases (δ5d).
supplementation of the maternal diets with fish oil or flaxseed oil increased the content of n-3 PUFAs in the female piglets' muscles and adipose tissue.
supplementation of the maternal diets with fish oil or with linseed oil increased n-3 PUFAs in female piglets in a specific tissue-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of n-3 fatty-acid supplementation on lipogenesis in female piglets.
the effect of the maternal diet supplemented with n-3 PUFAs on fatty-acid content and lipogenic enzyme expression in the female piglet.
the effect of the maternal diet on the expression of the lipogenesis-related enzymes in the progeny and the fatty-acid profile in different tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supplementation of the maternal pig diet with n-6 or n-3 PUFAs affects the fatty-acids composition of the female piglets in a sex-specific manner, but not by the same extent in all tissues.
the expression of Δ5d is tissue-specific in piglets, whereas that of Δ6d is tissue-specific and sex-dependent.

supplementation of the maternal pig diet with n- 3 PUFA affects the fatty-acids composition in the female progeny via enhancing of expression and activity of Δ5d, Δ6d and other lipogenic enzymes in the piglets tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the n-3 PUAs are beneficial for the offspring, and the effect is tissue specific.
the n-3 PU FA content in the maternal diet affects the fatty-acids composition of the piglets' muscles, subcutaneous and perirenal adipose tissue and livers, and the effect is tissue-specific.
dietary supplementation with fish oil or flaxseed oil in sows, which are fed during gestation, is a good way to increase n-3 PUFAs in the progeny.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supplementation of maternal diets with n-3 PUFAs can be an effective way to increase n-3 PUFU content in the offspring.

supplementation of the maternal diets with fish oil and linseed oil affects the fatty-acids profile in female piglets via activation of Δ5d, and to a lesser extent Δ6d, expression in the piglets tissues, with the highest response observed in the muscle.
the fatty-acid content in the piglets can be modified by maternal diet.
